analysis.objective: Close the ADR-0015 accepted-change record loop for Breaking Changes. Dev accept-schema (CLI and the dev-only MCP tool) saves dev's new baseline and also writes a committed pipelines/accepted/ record. accept-schema --env stage|prod becomes read-only and writes only the record file. A new CLI-only accept-schema --branch <name> hand-accepts a Branch Environment's baseline under stage's Warehouse lock. analysis.successDefinition: Done when ALL of these hold. (1) `adops accept-schema <pipeline> <table>` in dev does what it does today: same Breaking Change detection, same dropped-column NOT NULL relaxation, saves dev's snapshot, takes no lock. When it found Breaking Changes, it also creates exactly one pipelines/accepted/<id>.yaml record. The id is built from a seconds-precision UTC timestamp plus the pipeline and table. The record lists the changes in BreakingChange.message wording, loads through the h13 record loader and passes `adops validate`. It prints the record path. (2) The MCP accept_schema tool in dev does the same and returns the record path in its reply. It still refuses every Environment other than dev, takes no lock, and its reply carries no secret (assert_no_secret). (3) Before writing, if an existing pipelines/accepted/ record already lists the same changes for the same Pipeline table, it prints that record's path and creates no new file. A new record is created exclusively (O_EXCL-style): if the file name already exists it refuses with a clean error and never overwrites. (4) `--env stage|prod` reads that Environment's snapshot and Source and writes only the record file. A unit test proves no snapshot save, no relaxation and no applied-record write happen. It does not write dlt state, schemas or tables in that Warehouse. If there is no previous snapshot or no Breaking Change, it writes no file and gives a plain message. (5) `adops accept-schema --branch <name>` (CLI only; mutually exclusive with --env) works like dev's accept-schema against the Branch layout (br_<name>__ schemas, br_<name>__adops snapshot) using the stage_branch_name derivation. It runs under stage's Warehouse lock with the CLI's 30-minute wait, and writes no record file. The MCP tool still refuses Branch schema acceptance. (6) The Docker demo E2E, on both Postgres and DuckDB, runs this scenario and stays inside the 20-minute job: a Source column drop makes the stage run halt; dev accept-schema writes a record; the next stage run applies it and names it in the Step result; a further stage run does not apply it again. (7) ADR-0015 and ADR-0014 text matches the shipped behaviour, including the stale ADR-0014 'horizon 8' pointer. GLOSSARY gains accept-schema / accepted-change record entries if they are missing. decisions.md gets dated supersession lines for h2 'accepted only via accept-schema --env', h6 'accept-schema --branch is a known gap' and h13 'until horizon 14 it still writes directly'. (8) Repo gates pass: ruff, 100% line+branch coverage on src/adops with no new pragma, domain/application purity tests, the template wheel list check, unit and E2E suites.

The duplicate check depends on exact text matching between the changes found now and BreakingChange.message wording in existing records. A difference in wording (the parenthesised retyped form, or an empty previous_type for dropped columns in parse_change) could produce duplicates or false matches.
An exclusive-create refusal on a same-second collision gives a user-visible failure in a rare race (two machines, or quick retries). It is acceptable by user choice but could confuse users.

Dev accept-schema writes a record from dev's view while dev's Source may differ from prod's. A record built in dev may not cover what stage/prod actually see, so stage halts naming the uncovered changes. That is the intended h13 behaviour, but users may find it surprising.
--branch takes stage's single exclusive Warehouse lock (one lock per Warehouse, not per Pipeline). A long stage run makes the CLI wait up to 30 minutes and then fail.
Existing unit tests assert that --env stage writes the Warehouse (test_accept_schema_command.py ~317-345). They must be rewritten, not deleted, or coverage and behaviour drift.
Adding methods to @runtime_checkable ports (for example a read-only lookup) breaks isinstance tests on every real adapter until each adapter implements them.
Records are discovered by Pipeline name, but nothing enforces a Pipeline's name == its file stem. A record written under pipeline.name could be cross-checked against the wrong file by validate.

Writing pipelines/accepted/ from the MCP tool must stay inside the edit/write boundary rules (pipelines/ only; adops.yaml/.env/.adops refused). A wrong path join could let a crafted table name escape the folder. Table names must be checked to be plain names before they go into the id.

analysis.domainShapeReason: The objective encodes DataOps rules a data-engineering expert recognizes: a Breaking Change is accepted only deliberately, records are promoted through Git and applied once per Environment, stage/prod are read-only for acceptance, and Branch Environments are hand-accepted.

ubiquitousLanguage.meaning: A dropped or retyped Source column, compared with an Environment's saved schema snapshot, that halts the Sync Step and every later Step.

A committed pipelines/accepted/<id>.yaml file listing the accepted dropped/retyped changes of one Pipeline table, applied at most once by stage, prod and Branch Sync Steps.
A record id stored in an Environment's _adops_applied_records table, together with its snapshot, so the record never applies again in that Environment.
The saved baseline shape of a Sync table in an Environment's adops schema (adops or br_<name>__adops), against which Breaking Changes are found.
A named target (dev, stage, prod) with its own Warehouse, or a Branch Environment in stage's Warehouse under br_<name>__ schemas.
The single exclusive per-Warehouse lock (Postgres advisory lock or DuckDB flock) that Warehouse-writing runs take; --branch takes stage's, with the CLI's 30-minute wait.
Making the Warehouse columns of a dropped Source column nullable when a change is accepted, so later loads do not fail on a constraint.

phases.name: Split accept-schema into find and save steps
phases.goal: The accept-schema use case has a read-only step that finds a Pipeline table's Breaking Changes against the Environment's schema snapshot, a separate step that applies the dropped-column NOT NULL relaxation and saves the new baseline, and a pure rule that decides which accepted-change record (if any) to write.
phases.rationale: Today one function finds Breaking Changes, alters the Warehouse and saves the snapshot together, so stage and prod cannot use it without writing, and it cannot target a Branch Environment because it looks the Environment up by name in adops.yaml. Splitting it lets dev, --branch and the read-only --env path share the same finding logic. The record decision (no change, already covered, or a new record) is a business rule, so it lives here over existing domain pieces rather than in the CLI.
changes: Add find_schema_changes(pipeline_text, settings_text, settings_environment_name, table, env, sync, snapshot_store) that loads the Pipeline, picks the settings Environment, runs sync.preflight and snapshot_store.load and find_breaking_changes, and returns a frozen FoundSchemaChanges (pipeline, step, source, table, shape, warehouse, previous-snapshot-present flag, changes); it never calls relax_dropped_columns or save.

Keep accept_schema as find + relax_dropped_columns + snapshot_store.save, taking the settings Environment name apart from the reported environment name so a Branch (br_<name>) can use stage's Sources and Warehouse secrets.
Add a changes field to AcceptedSchema so callers can build a record from what was found.

Add plan_accepted_record(pipeline_name, table, changes, existing_records, now) returning one of: nothing to record (no changes), already covered (ids of existing records for the same Pipeline table when cover() with applied_ids=() leaves no change uncovered), or a new AcceptedChangeRecord listing EVERY change found (not only the uncovered ones) whose id is <now formatted with TIMESTAMP_FORMAT>-<Pipeline.name>-<table>.

Expose a named apply step apply_schema_acceptance(found, sync, snapshot_store) that runs relax_dropped_columns and snapshot_store.save; accept_schema = find_schema_changes + apply_schema_acceptance, so the interface can run find -> plan -> write record -> apply and a refused record leaves dev's baseline unchanged.
Refuse a table that is not a plain name (is_plain_name) with a PipelineValidationError before building the id.

Add unit tests for every branch: no previous snapshot, no change, fully covered by an existing record, partly covered (new record lists every found change — assert the exact list), non-plain table, Branch environment name reported while stage settings are used.

rubric.label: find_schema_changes never writes
rubric.ruleStatement: find_schema_changes returns a frozen FoundSchemaChanges and never calls relax_dropped_columns, make_columns_nullable or snapshot_store.save; the write happens only in the separate apply step. 10 = a recording fake proves zero write calls on every branch including the changes-found branch; 8 = proven on the changes-found branch; minScore is the acceptable bar.
passCriteria: In tests/unit/application/test_accept_schema.py, a test calls find_schema_changes with a seeded previous snapshot and a dropped column and asserts the fake snapshot store recorded no save and the fake sync recorded no make_columns_nullable call.
`grep -n "save\|relax_dropped_columns\|make_columns_nullable" src/adops/application/accept_schema.py` shows those calls only inside the apply/accept_schema function, not inside find_schema_changes.
FoundSchemaChanges is a @dataclass(frozen=True) carrying the previous-snapshot-present flag and the changes tuple.
apply_schema_acceptance exists in src/adops/application/accept_schema.py and is the only function there that calls relax_dropped_columns or snapshot_store.save.
failureExamples: find_schema_changes reuses the old accept_schema body and calls relax_dropped_columns 'only when changes exist', so the read path still alters the Warehouse.
FoundSchemaChanges is a plain mutable dataclass and the changes field is a list.

rubric.label: plan_accepted_record returns the right one of three outcomes
rubric.ruleStatement: plan_accepted_record returns nothing-to-record for no changes, already-covered (with the covering record ids) when cover(..., applied_ids=()) leaves no change uncovered for the same Pipeline table, and otherwise a new AcceptedChangeRecord listing EVERY found change. 10 = each outcome plus a record for a different table that must not count as covering is tested with exact equality; 8 = the three outcomes and the partial-cover case are tested with exact equality.
passCriteria: A unit test with a partly covering existing record asserts the new record's changes equal the full tuple of found changes, compared with ==, not only the uncovered subset.
A unit test with a fully covering existing record asserts the result is the already-covered outcome and its ids equal the covering record id(s).
A unit test with an existing record for a different table of the same Pipeline asserts it is not treated as covering.
A unit test with no changes asserts the nothing-to-record outcome.
failureExamples: The partly covered case writes a record with only the uncovered changes, so stage later finds the earlier change applied in one Environment but not another.
Covering is checked across all records of the Pipeline regardless of table, so a record for 'customers' suppresses a new record for 'orders'.

rubric.label: Record id format and non-plain table refusal
rubric.ruleStatement: A new record's id is exactly <now formatted with TIMESTAMP_FORMAT>-<Pipeline.name>-<table>, built from a passed-in time, and a table that fails is_plain_name raises PipelineValidationError before any id is built. 10 = the id is asserted as a literal string and a path-traversal table such as '../x' is refused; 8 = id asserted literally and one non-plain table refused.
passCriteria: A unit test passes a fixed datetime and asserts the record id equals a literal string such as '<formatted time>-shop_sync-orders'.
A unit test passes table='../orders' (or another non-plain name) and asserts PipelineValidationError via pytest.raises.
`grep -n "\.now(" src/adops/application/accept_schema.py` returns nothing.
failureExamples: The id uses datetime.isoformat() instead of TIMESTAMP_FORMAT, so it contains ':' and differs from existing record ids.
The table check runs after the id string is built and only rejects an empty name, letting 'a/b' through.

rubric.label: Settings Environment kept apart from reported Environment
rubric.ruleStatement: accept_schema and find_schema_changes take a settings Environment name (whose Sources and Warehouse secrets are used) separately from the reported Environment name, so a Branch reports br_<name> while using stage settings. 10 = a test asserts both the settings looked up and the name in the result; 8 = one test proves a Branch name is reported while stage settings are used.
passCriteria: A unit test calls accept_schema with settings_environment_name='stage' and env='br_feat' and asserts the result's environment is 'br_feat' and the fake sync was preflighted with stage's Source settings.
No code path in src/adops/application/accept_schema.py looks up a 'br_'-prefixed name in adops.yaml settings.
failureExamples: The settings Environment is derived by stripping 'br_' from env inside the application, hard-coding the Branch naming rule in two places.
A single env parameter is kept and the Branch case is left to fail with an unknown-Environment error.

rubric.label: Record decision lives in the application layer without IO
rubric.ruleStatement: The record decision and find/apply split live in src/adops/application/accept_schema.py using only stdlib datetime/dataclasses, adops.domain and adops.application; no file path, YAML writing or clock read. 10 = no Path, open or yaml import anywhere in the module; 8 = no IO and the time comes in as a parameter.
passCriteria: `grep -nE "^(import|from) " src/adops/application/accept_schema.py` lists only stdlib (datetime, dataclasses, typing, collections.abc), adops.domain.* and adops.application.* modules.
`grep -nE "open\(|Path\(|pathlib|yaml" src/adops/application/accept_schema.py` returns nothing.
plan_accepted_record takes existing_records and now as parameters rather than loading them.
failureExamples: plan_accepted_record calls load_project_records(project) itself, pulling interface file loading into the application layer.
The application module imports pathlib to compute the record file name pipelines/accepted/<id>.yaml.

phases.healerHint: The likeliest miss is a partly covered table producing a record with only the uncovered changes or with a non-TIMESTAMP_FORMAT id; fix plan_accepted_record to emit found.changes verbatim and build the id with now.strftime(TIMESTAMP_FORMAT), then assert both with == in the unit test.

phases.name: Add read-only mode to the snapshot store
phases.goal: A WarehouseSnapshotStore built read-only loads an Environment's schema snapshot without creating the adops schema, without CREATE TABLE and without creating .adops/dlt/<env> local state; a missing schema or snapshot table reads as no previous snapshot.
phases.rationale: Every snapshot store call today creates the adops dataset, both adops tables and dlt local state, so even reading a stage or prod snapshot writes to that Warehouse. Stage and prod must be read-only for accept-schema. A constructor option on the existing adapter keeps the shared SchemaSnapshotStore port unchanged, so no fake or isinstance check breaks.
changes: Add a keyword-only read_only: bool = False to WarehouseSnapshotStore.__init__.

In read-only mode, point dlt at a throwaway temporary pipelines_dir instead of local_state_dir(project, environment), skip create_dataset and both CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS statements, and return None from load() when the dataset or the snapshot table is missing.
Make save() refuse in read-only mode with a clear error so a wiring mistake cannot write.

On DuckDB, a read-only load never creates a missing Warehouse file (check the file exists first; missing file = no previous snapshot) and opens an existing file read-only; on Postgres it issues no DDL.
Add a read_only keyword to run_command.build_snapshot_store that passes through.

Add infrastructure tests on DuckDB proving a read-only load on a missing Warehouse file returns None and does not create the file, on an empty Warehouse returns None and leaves no adops schema, no tables and no .adops/dlt/<env> directory, and reads an existing snapshot correctly; plus a Postgres test (ADOPS_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN) that no adops schema is created.
phases.expectedResult: tests/unit/infrastructure/test_schema_snapshot_store.py passes with read-only tests proving load() creates no Warehouse file, no schema, no table and no .adops/dlt/<env> directory.
guardNotes: g2: the read-only branches (missing dataset, missing table, save refused) each have a real test; no pragma.
g5: change is in infrastructure only; domain/application untouched.
phases.compensation: The option defaults to False, so removing it restores today's behaviour with no data effect.

rubric.label: Read-only load leaves the Warehouse untouched
rubric.ruleStatement: A WarehouseSnapshotStore built with read_only=True issues no create_dataset and no CREATE TABLE, and on DuckDB never creates a missing Warehouse file. 10 = both DuckDB cases (missing file, empty file) and the Postgres case are tested and assert schema and file absence afterward; 8 = both DuckDB cases tested and Postgres test present behind ADOPS_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN.
passCriteria: A test in tests/unit/infrastructure/test_schema_snapshot_store.py calls load() read-only on a DuckDB path that does not exist, asserts None, and asserts the path still does not exist.
A test on an existing empty DuckDB file asserts load() returns None and information_schema shows no 'adops' schema and no adops tables afterward.
A Postgres test gated on ADOPS_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN asserts no adops schema exists after a read-only load.
Run `uv run pytest tests/unit/infrastructure/test_schema_snapshot_store.py -q` and see all tests pass.
failureExamples: load() skips CREATE TABLE but dlt's destination client still creates the dataset on first connection, so the adops schema appears in stage.
duckdb.connect(path) is called before the existence check, silently creating an empty Warehouse file.

rubric.label: No .adops/dlt/<env> local state in read-only mode
rubric.ruleStatement: Read-only mode points dlt at a throwaway temporary pipelines_dir instead of local_state_dir(project, environment), so no .adops/dlt/<env> directory appears. 10 = the test also asserts the temporary directory is cleaned up; 8 = the test asserts .adops/dlt/<env> is absent after load.
passCriteria: A test runs a read-only load in a tmp project and asserts (project / '.adops' / 'dlt' / env).exists() is False.
`grep -n "local_state_dir" src/adops/infrastructure/schema_snapshot_store.py` shows it is not used on the read_only branch.
failureExamples: The temporary dir is created under the project's .adops folder, so a .adops/dlt/... tree still appears in the repo.
Only the dataset DDL is skipped; local state is still written to .adops/dlt/stage.

rubric.label: Existing snapshot reads correctly and save() refuses
rubric.ruleStatement: Read-only load returns the same snapshot a writable store saved, and save() on a read-only store raises a clear error before any connection. 10 = the round trip compares the whole snapshot with == and the save test asserts the Warehouse is unchanged; 8 = round trip equality and save refusal with a message match.
passCriteria: A test saves a snapshot with a writable store, then loads it with read_only=True and asserts equality with the saved snapshot.
A test calls save() on a read-only store and asserts pytest.raises with a message naming read-only.
Missing-table case: a DuckDB file with an adops schema but no snapshot table makes load() return None.
failureExamples: save() in read-only mode silently returns, so a wiring mistake goes unnoticed.
The read-only load opens DuckDB with read_only=True but the missing-table case raises CatalogException instead of returning None.

rubric.label: Option stays on the adapter; port and default behaviour unchanged
rubric.ruleStatement: read_only is a keyword-only constructor option on WarehouseSnapshotStore defaulting to False, the SchemaSnapshotStore port signature is unchanged, and run_command.build_snapshot_store passes it through. 10 = existing writable tests pass unmodified; 8 = port unchanged and factory passes the flag.
passCriteria: `git diff -- src/adops/domain src/adops/application` shows no change to the SchemaSnapshotStore protocol.
`grep -n "read_only" src/adops/interface/run_command.py` shows build_snapshot_store accepting a read_only keyword and forwarding it.
WarehouseSnapshotStore.__init__ declares read_only after a '*' so it cannot be passed positionally.
failureExamples: A new ReadOnlySnapshotStore port is added to the domain, forcing every fake in tests/unit/application/fakes.py to change.
read_only is positional, shifting an existing argument and breaking a caller.

phases.healerHint: The likeliest failure is dlt or duckdb.connect creating the dataset or file before the read-only check; fix by testing Path.exists() first, opening DuckDB with read_only=True, and querying information_schema directly instead of going through dlt's create path.

phases.name: Write accepted-change record from CLI accept-schema
phases.goal: adops accept-schema in dev saves dev's baseline as today and, when it found Breaking Changes, writes exactly one pipelines/accepted/<id>.yaml record and prints its path; with --env naming any other Environment it reads that Environment's snapshot and Source read-only and writes only the record file.
phases.rationale: The accepted-change record is how a deliberately accepted Breaking Change reaches stage and prod through Git, but nothing writes it yet. Dev keeps saving its own baseline lock-free; every other Environment named with --env must not touch its Warehouse. The record writer must never overwrite a committed record and must stay inside the pipelines folder.
changes: Make accept_project_schema return an outcome carrying the AcceptedSchema (dev) or FoundSchemaChanges (other Environments) plus record_path: Path | None and the ids of existing covering records.

Dev path, in this order: find_schema_changes, plan_accepted_record with load_project_records(project) and run_command.build_clock().now(), create the record file exclusively, THEN relax + save dev's baseline (no lock) — so a refused record (name clash, non-plain table) leaves dev unchanged and a re-run can still record.

Non-dev --env path (stage, prod, ci or any other name): call find_schema_changes with build_snapshot_store(..., read_only=True); never call accept_schema, make_columns_nullable, save or the applied-record write; no lock.

Write a new record with dump_accepted_record into PIPELINES_DIR/ACCEPTED_RECORDS_DIR, resolving the path through resolve_project_file(write=True) and opening it with mode 'x'; create the accepted folder if missing.
Add a RecordExists error (a ProjectFileError subclass) raised on a name clash and caught by the command with a clean message, never an overwrite.

Print: the record path when written; the existing record path(s) when already covered; 'no record written' when there was no previous snapshot or no Breaking Change (plain message, exit 0, for non-dev).
Change test fixtures to accept the layout/read_only keywords (lambda *_, **__).

Rewrite test_accept_schema_in_stage_uses_stage_local_state_and_finds_stage_snapshot and the env/kind tests to assert --env stage and --env ci write only the record: no save, no make_columns_nullable, no applied-record write, no .adops/dlt/<env> directory.
Add tests: dev writes a record that load_project_records loads and validate_project accepts; duplicate prints the existing path and writes nothing; clash refuses cleanly; non-plain table refused.
Add a test that a record-name clash in dev leaves dev's snapshot unsaved and no column relaxed.
inputs: find_schema_changes, accept_schema and plan_accepted_record from phase split-accept-schema-find-and-save
WarehouseSnapshotStore read_only option from phase add-read-only-snapshot-store
phases.expectedResult: tests/unit/interface/test_accept_schema_command.py passes, including a test that --env stage writes only a pipelines/accepted/<id>.yaml record and a test that dev writes a record that passes validate_project.
guardNotes: g2: each new branch (dev record, non-dev record, covered, clash, no snapshot, no change, non-plain table) is covered by a unit test; no pragma.
g5: file writes, Path handling and the clock read stay in the interface; domain/application gain no IO or framework import.

rubric.label: Dev writes one loadable record and prints its path
rubric.ruleStatement: Dev accept-schema with a Breaking Change writes exactly one pipelines/accepted/<id>.yaml that load_project_records loads and validate_project accepts, and prints that path. 10 = the test asserts the printed path, file count == 1, loader result and validate_project; 8 = file loads and validates and the path is printed.
passCriteria: A test in tests/unit/interface/test_accept_schema_command.py runs accept-schema in dev with a seeded snapshot and a dropped column, then asserts exactly one file matches pipelines/accepted/*.yaml.
The same test asserts load_project_records(project) returns a record whose changes match the dropped column and validate_project raises nothing.
The CLI output contains the project-relative record path.
failureExamples: The record is written with yaml.safe_dump of a dict instead of dump_accepted_record, so load_accepted_record rejects an unknown key.
The record is written to <cwd>/pipelines/accepted rather than the project's folder when the CLI runs from a subdirectory.

rubric.label: Record is created before dev's baseline changes
rubric.ruleStatement: On dev the record file is created with an exclusive open before relax + save, so a refused record (name clash, non-plain table) leaves dev's snapshot unsaved and no column relaxed. 10 = clash and non-plain table both proven to leave dev unchanged; 8 = clash proven to leave no save and no make_columns_nullable call.
passCriteria: A test pre-creates the record file with the expected id, runs dev accept-schema, and asserts a non-zero exit with a clean message, the fake store recorded no save, and the fake sync recorded no make_columns_nullable.
A test asserts the pre-existing record file's contents are byte-identical after the refused run.
`grep -n "'x'\|\"x\"" src/adops/interface/accept_schema_command.py` shows the record opened with mode 'x'.
failureExamples: The command saves dev's snapshot first and writes the record last, so a clash leaves dev accepted with no record and a re-run finds nothing to record.
The file is opened with 'w' after an exists() check, a race that can overwrite a committed record.

rubric.label: --env <non-dev> writes only the record
rubric.ruleStatement: For --env stage, prod, ci or any non-dev Environment, the command uses build_snapshot_store(..., read_only=True) and find_schema_changes only: no save, no make_columns_nullable, no applied-record write, no lock, no .adops/dlt/<env>. 10 = asserted for stage and for a custom-named Environment; 8 = asserted for stage and ci.
passCriteria: A test runs accept-schema --env stage with a dropped column and asserts a record file exists, the fake store recorded no save and no applied-record write, the fake sync recorded no make_columns_nullable, and no .adops/dlt/stage directory exists.
A test captures the build_snapshot_store call and asserts read_only=True was passed for --env stage.
A test with --env ci asserts the same write-only-record behaviour.
A non-dev run with no previous snapshot prints 'no record written' and exits 0.
failureExamples: The non-dev check is env == 'stage' or env == 'prod', so --env ci still saves a baseline in ci's Warehouse.
build_snapshot_store is called without read_only for non-dev, so the read creates the adops schema in stage.

rubric.label: Duplicate prints the existing record; writes stay inside pipelines
rubric.ruleStatement: When existing records already cover every found change the command writes nothing and prints the existing record path(s); new paths resolve through resolve_project_file(write=True) and a name clash raises RecordExists (a ProjectFileError subclass) with a clean message. 10 = duplicate, clash and a missing accepted folder are all tested; 8 = duplicate and clash tested.
passCriteria: A test runs dev accept-schema twice on the same change and asserts the second run prints the first record's path and the pipelines/accepted file count is still 1.
A test asserts issubclass(RecordExists, ProjectFileError) and that a clash produces a message without a Python traceback in CLI output.
A test with no pipelines/accepted folder asserts the folder is created and the record written.
failureExamples: The second run writes a second record with a newer timestamp, so stage applies the same change twice under two ids.
RecordExists escapes as an uncaught FileExistsError traceback.

rubric.label: Interface holds IO and clock, not the record rule
rubric.ruleStatement: The interface reads the clock via run_command.build_clock().now(), loads records and writes the file, but delegates the record decision to plan_accepted_record; it does not re-implement covering or id building. 10 = no cover() call and no TIMESTAMP_FORMAT use in the interface module; 8 = decision delegated with no duplicate id logic.
passCriteria: `grep -nE "cover\(|TIMESTAMP_FORMAT|strftime" src/adops/interface/accept_schema_command.py` returns nothing.
`grep -n "plan_accepted_record" src/adops/interface/accept_schema_command.py` shows it called on the dev and non-dev paths.
failureExamples: The command builds the file name with datetime.now().strftime itself, so the id can disagree with the record's own id.
The command checks coverage by comparing file names in pipelines/accepted instead of using plan_accepted_record.

phases.healerHint: The likeliest failure is ordering: saving dev's baseline before the exclusive record write, or treating only stage/prod as read-only; fix by running find -> plan -> open(path, 'x') -> relax + save, and branching on env != 'dev' with read_only=True.

phases.name: Add accept-schema --branch under stage's lock
phases.goal: adops accept-schema --branch <name> hand-accepts a Branch Environment's baseline exactly like dev's accept-schema (detection, dropped-column NOT NULL relaxation, snapshot save in br_<name>__adops) using stage's settings Environment, while holding stage's Warehouse lock with the CLI's 30-minute wait, and writes no record file.
phases.rationale: A Branch Environment lives in stage's Warehouse under br_<name>__ schemas, and until now there was no way to accept a Breaking Change there by hand. It writes to stage's Warehouse, so it must take stage's single Warehouse lock like drop-branch does. A Branch is hand-accepted, so no record file is written.
changes: Add a --branch option; reject it together with --env using the same BadParameter text run uses.

Derive the Branch name with stage_branch_name(stage, branch) and build adapters with build_sync(..., layout=SchemaLayout.for_branch(name)) and build_snapshot_store(..., layout=SchemaLayout.for_branch(name)).

Call accept_schema with settings Environment stage and reported environment br_<name>, inside 'with run_command.build_warehouse_lock(warehouse, project, STAGE, DEFAULT_LOCK_TIMEOUT)' as drop_branch_command does.
Never call plan_accepted_record or the record writer on this path; print the accepted shape and relaxed columns.
Catch WarehouseLocked and WarehouseUnreachable with clean messages.
Add tests: Branch layout used, stage settings used, lock taken on stage with the 30-minute default, WarehouseLocked message, --env with --branch refused, no file under pipelines/accepted.
inputs: accept_schema with separate settings Environment from phase split-accept-schema-find-and-save
accept_project_schema outcome and keyword-tolerant test fixtures (lambda *_, **__) from phase write-record-from-cli-accept-schema
phases.expectedResult: A unit test in tests/unit/interface/test_accept_schema_command.py proves accept-schema --branch feat saves the snapshot under the br_feat layout while holding stage's Warehouse lock with the 30-minute wait and writes no record file.
guardNotes: g2: lock taken, lock timeout, --env/--branch exclusion and unreachable Warehouse each have a test; no pragma.

rubric.label: --branch holds stage's Warehouse lock with the 30-minute wait
rubric.ruleStatement: accept-schema --branch <name> runs accept_schema inside run_command.build_warehouse_lock(warehouse, project, STAGE, DEFAULT_LOCK_TIMEOUT), the same pattern as drop_branch_command. 10 = the test asserts the lock was held at the moment save was called; 8 = the test asserts the lock was taken on stage with the default timeout.
passCriteria: A test in tests/unit/interface/test_accept_schema_command.py replaces build_warehouse_lock with a recording fake and asserts it was called with environment 'stage' and timeout DEFAULT_LOCK_TIMEOUT (30 minutes).
A test asserts the snapshot save happened while the fake lock was entered and not yet exited.
A test where the lock raises WarehouseLocked asserts a clean message, a non-zero exit and no save.
failureExamples: The lock is taken on the Branch name 'br_feat', so a concurrent stage run is not excluded.
The lock is taken with a zero or MCP-style short timeout instead of the CLI's 30-minute default.

rubric.label: Branch layout and stage settings are used
rubric.ruleStatement: The Branch name comes from stage_branch_name(stage, branch); build_sync and build_snapshot_store receive layout=SchemaLayout.for_branch(name); accept_schema gets settings Environment stage and reported environment br_<name>. 10 = the test asserts the snapshot lands in br_<name>__adops and the output names br_<name>; 8 = both factories asserted to receive the Branch layout and stage settings.
passCriteria: A test runs accept-schema --branch feat and asserts both build_sync and build_snapshot_store were called with layout == SchemaLayout.for_branch('br_feat') (or whatever stage_branch_name returns).
The same test asserts accept_schema received settings Environment 'stage' and environment 'br_feat'.
CLI output names the Branch Environment and lists the relaxed columns.
failureExamples: Only build_snapshot_store gets the Branch layout, so relax_dropped_columns alters stage's own tables instead of br_feat__ tables.
The name is built as f'br_{branch}' by hand, ignoring stage_branch_name's normalisation.

rubric.label: Branch acceptance writes no record
rubric.ruleStatement: The --branch path never calls plan_accepted_record or the record writer. 10 = asserted both by an empty pipelines/accepted folder and by a spy on plan_accepted_record; 8 = no file under pipelines/accepted after a run with a dropped column.
passCriteria: A test runs accept-schema --branch feat with a dropped column and asserts no file matches pipelines/accepted/*.yaml.
A test spies on plan_accepted_record and asserts it is not called during accept-schema --branch.
failureExamples: --branch reuses the dev path wholesale and writes a record, which stage would then apply to its own tables.

rubric.label: --env with --branch refused; unreachable Warehouse handled
rubric.ruleStatement: --branch together with --env is refused with the same BadParameter text run uses, and WarehouseUnreachable produces a clean message. 10 = the exact text is asserted equal to run's; 8 = both cases tested with message checks.
passCriteria: A test runs accept-schema --branch feat --env stage and asserts exit code 2 and the same error text the run command emits for --env with --branch.
A test makes the Warehouse unreachable and asserts a clean one-line message with no traceback.
failureExamples: --env is silently ignored when --branch is given, so a user typing --env prod --branch x gets a stage Branch acceptance.
The exclusion message is reworded and diverges from run's.

phases.healerHint: The likeliest failure is passing the Branch layout to only one adapter or taking the lock on br_<name> instead of stage; fix by copying drop_branch_command's build_warehouse_lock(..., STAGE, DEFAULT_LOCK_TIMEOUT) wrapper and passing SchemaLayout.for_branch(name) to both build_sync and build_snapshot_store.

phases.name: Return record path from MCP accept_schema
phases.goal: The dev-only MCP accept_schema tool returns the written accepted-change record's path in an optional record_path reply field, names covering existing records in covered_by, and its Branch refusal text points the user to the CLI accept-schema --branch.
phases.rationale: This is one small slice across layers: a reply field in the MCP interface and one refusal sentence in the domain's Assistant access rules. The MCP tool already calls the CLI's accept_project_schema, so it writes the record once the CLI phase lands, but the Assistant cannot see where the record went. The old refusal says a Branch has nothing to accept, which is no longer true.
changes: Add record_path: str | None (project-relative path of the newly written record, None when none was written) and covered_by: list[str] (project-relative paths of existing records that already cover the found changes, empty otherwise) to AcceptedSchemaReply and fill both in accepted_schema_reply from the accept_project_schema outcome.

Add a test proving a RecordExists clash passes through _sanitized_errors with its message (RecordExists is a ProjectFileError subclass, and ProjectFileError is already in RUN_ERRORS, so no RUN_ERRORS edit is needed).
Reword ACCEPT_SCHEMA_DEV_ONLY so Branch acceptance points to 'adops accept-schema --branch <name>' run by hand.

Update test_mcp_server.py: add record_path to the expected structuredContent (None with no previous snapshot), add a seeded dropped-column test that asserts a pipelines/accepted/*.yaml file is created and its path returned, update the Branch refusal text assertion, keep assert_no_secret and the no-lock assertion.
inputs: accept_project_schema outcome with record_path from phase write-record-from-cli-accept-schema
phases.expectedResult: tests/unit/interface/test_mcp_server.py passes with a test where MCP accept_schema in dev returns record_path naming a newly created pipelines/accepted/<id>.yaml file and takes no lock.

g5: the domain change is a string constant only; no framework import enters domain.

rubric.label: record_path reply field is set or None
rubric.ruleStatement: AcceptedSchemaReply has record_path: str | None, filled with the project-relative path of the written record (None when none was written), and covered_by: list[str] naming existing covering records. 10 = the set-path test also asserts the file exists and loads with load_project_records, and the covered case is tested; 8 = None, set and covered cases all asserted in structuredContent.
passCriteria: In tests/unit/interface/test_mcp_server.py, the no-previous-snapshot test asserts structuredContent['record_path'] is None.
A seeded dropped-column test asserts structuredContent['record_path'] starts with 'pipelines/accepted/' and ends with '.yaml', and (project / record_path).exists() is True.
The returned path is relative (no leading '/' and no absolute tmp path).

A test calls MCP accept_schema twice on the same dropped column and asserts the second reply has record_path None, covered_by equal to [the first reply's record_path], and still exactly one file under pipelines/accepted/.

The already-covered case returns record_path None and an empty covered_by, so the Assistant cannot tell 'covered by record X' from 'nothing to record'.

rubric.label: RecordExists reaches the Assistant with its message
rubric.ruleStatement: RecordExists is in RUN_ERRORS so _sanitized_errors passes its text to the Assistant, with no secret leaked. 10 = a clash test asserts the message text and assert_no_secret; 8 = a clash test asserts isError and the message.

successCriteria: Done when ALL of these hold. (1) `adops accept-schema <pipeline> <table>` in dev does what it does today: same Breaking Change detection, same dropped-column NOT NULL relaxation, saves dev's snapshot, takes no lock. When it found Breaking Changes, it also creates exactly one pipelines/accepted/<id>.yaml record. The id is built from a seconds-precision UTC timestamp plus the pipeline and table. The record lists the changes in BreakingChange.message wording, loads through the h13 record loader and passes `adops validate`. It prints the record path. (2) The MCP accept_schema tool in dev does the same and returns the record path in its reply. It still refuses every Environment other than dev, takes no lock, and its reply carries no secret (assert_no_secret). (3) Before writing, if an existing pipelines/accepted/ record already lists the same changes for the same Pipeline table, it prints that record's path and creates no new file. A new record is created exclusively (O_EXCL-style): if the file name already exists it refuses with a clean error and never overwrites. (4) `--env stage|prod` reads that Environment's snapshot and Source and writes only the record file. A unit test proves no snapshot save, no relaxation and no applied-record write happen. It does not write dlt state, schemas or tables in that Warehouse. If there is no previous snapshot or no Breaking Change, it writes no file and gives a plain message. (5) `adops accept-schema --branch <name>` (CLI only; mutually exclusive with --env) works like dev's accept-schema against the Branch layout (br_<name>__ schemas, br_<name>__adops snapshot) using the stage_branch_name derivation. It runs under stage's Warehouse lock with the CLI's 30-minute wait, and writes no record file. The MCP tool still refuses Branch schema acceptance. (6) The Docker demo E2E, on both Postgres and DuckDB, runs this scenario and stays inside the 20-minute job: a Source column drop makes the stage run halt; dev accept-schema writes a record; the next stage run applies it and names it in the Step result; a further stage run does not apply it again. (7) ADR-0015 and ADR-0014 text matches the shipped behaviour, including the stale ADR-0014 'horizon 8' pointer. (8) Repo gates pass: ruff, 100% line+branch coverage on src/adops with no new pragma, domain/application purity tests, the template wheel list check, unit and E2E suites.
